title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft connected apps
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, licensing and meter, prerequisites, controls and preview limitations are supported. Two wizard paths need minor completion, but neither sends administrators to the wrong place. The briefing correctly preserves Microsoft's conflicting migration sequencing guidance and the gap between retirement and planned general availability.

claims.claim: The printed Purview DLP wizard path reaches Choose where to apply the policy through the documented policy-type, template and admin-unit steps.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy. ... On What info do you want to protect?, choose the Enterprise applications & devices option. ... On Choose where to apply the policy, select one or more of the supported non-Microsoft apps
claims.fix: Keep the existing path and append ' > app > Edit > Specific instances > + Include instance' to reach the instance-scoping control recommended by the checklist. This continuation is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-non-microsoft-connected-applications.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected apps dedicated locations New-DlpCompliancePolicy New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy PowerShell API Box GoogleWorkspace. Read DLP feature page and New-DlpCompliancePolicy; ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation links to legacy Instances, not dedicated app locations.

claims.claim: The printed auto-labeling route and its note follow documented wizard choices, but omit the policy-type page heading.
claims.quote: On What type of auto-labeling policy do you want to create?, choose Automatically apply labels only. ... On Choose a label to auto-apply, choose Choose a label. On Choose a sensitivity label, select all labels to include in the policy
claims.fix: Use 'Solutions > Information protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy > What type of auto-labeling policy do you want to create? > Automatically apply labels only > Custom > Custom policy > Choose a label to auto-apply > Choose a label > Choose a sensitivity label > Add > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose locations where you want to apply the label', retaining the existing note's qualifications. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-non-microsoft-connected-apps.

claims.quote: For more information about DLP for non-Microsoft cloud apps, see Use data loss prevention policies for non-Microsoft cloud apps.
